transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Giles Snyder.
Polls are closing this hour in California, Idaho, Oregon,
and Washington State, as voters across the country
are deciding control of the House of Representatives
and the Senate in this year's midterm elections.
So far, Democrats have flipped five House seats
and two in the Senate, the latest in South Carolina,
according to an Associated Press race call.
Democrat Annie Andrews won an upset victory
over Republican Darlene Graham in South Carolina.
Eric McDaniel covers Congress for NPR,
and Eric, what do you expect to see
if Democrats are able to take control
of at least one of the chambers of Congress?
- I mean, in short, less cooperation.
Trump has had a compliant Congress
under Republican control so far,
and Democrats have been champing at the bit
to investigate the president, his family,
his associates in the second term,
and that's on issues that span everything
from Trump's business entanglements while in office
to the extent of his relationship
with the late sex offender, Jeffrey Epstein.
But because of the special immunity claimed by the president
and granted to him by the Supreme Court,
it seems certain the administration will do everything
in their power to resist, but important to remember,
regardless of whether they flip one or both chambers,
Trump still controls the veto pen,
so legislating will be hard.
- Can you talk a little bit about the legislative priorities
from Democrats?
Should they contain, gain control of only one chamber?
- Sure, I mean, in the House, that seems most likely speaker,
future speaker, likely Hakeem Jeffries
will have lots of messaging bills on healthcare,
the social safety net, U.S. military support for Israel,
among other efforts, and a big effort
to end the war with Iran, with seven in 10 Americans
opposing it and it being the primary driver
of a high cost of living, which was a central issue
during this midterm campaign.
Democrats have, you know, what they call 100 hours agenda
and 100 days agenda, but again, it's all exceedingly
unlikely to become law with split control.
- Moving now to the battle for control
of governor's offices around the country,
the Associated Press has just called the race in Ohio
for Democrat Amy Acton over Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.
In Georgia, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms
is said to become the state and country's first black woman
to be elected governor.
The Associated Press called that race
after Democrat John Ossoff won reelection
to his Georgia Senate seat.
Here's NPR's Sam Greenglass reporting.
Ossoff is the only incumbent Senate Democrat
defending a seat in a state President Trump carried in 2024.
- The American people have rebuked the depravity,
corruption, and incompetence
of the failed lame duck President Donald J. Trump.
- But in Collins, the GOP in Georgia nominated a candidate
with a lot of personal baggage, and in Ossoff,
Democrats were buoyed by a candidate who won respect at home
even from some Republican officials
for the strength of his constituent services.
And outside Georgia, Ossoff electrified Democrats
searching for fresh faces to lead the party
out of the political wilderness.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News.
- And you're listening to NPR News.
Federal safety investigators have confirmed
that the business jet that crashed in South Florida
Sunday afternoon was breaking apart before it came down.
The National Transportation Safety Board
says three pieces of the jet have been found
between 1.3 and 3.8 miles away from the main crash site.
The plane crashed into a residential area near West Palm Beach.
Nine people on board were killed.
A gallon of gasoline costs over $4.
A diesel's not far from its record high in September,
which was above $6.50.
As companies report their profits this quarter,
the nation's biggest oil refiner told investors
it raked in sky-high revenue.
Here's NPR's Willow Rubin.
Marathon Petroleum Corporation made more than
$7 billion this quarter.
That's about seven times what it made this time last year.
Most of its money came from refining,
turning crude oil into stuff we use,
gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, other plastics.
Marathon's operating costs were flat
compared to this time last year.
But the war in Iran and Ukrainian strikes
on Russian refineries have reduced how much gas
and diesel has gotten to global markets raising prices.
On Marathon's earnings call, executives said gas
and diesel inventories are still relatively low,
and they expect the high margins on refining
to continue well into next year.
Marathon said it's raising its quarterly dividend
to investors 10%.
Willow Rubin, NPR News.
- On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average
closed down 197 points today to 51,786.
I'm Jael Snyder.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Democrats flip five House seats and two Senate seats so far, per AP race calls
Democrat Annie Andrews upsets Republican Darlene Graham in South Carolina
NPR's Eric McDaniel on what Democratic control of Congress would mean for Trump
AP calls Ohio governor's race for Democrat Amy Acton over Vivek Ramaswamy
Keisha Lance Bottoms projected to become Georgia's first Black woman governor
Democrat Jon Ossoff wins reelection to Georgia Senate seat, NPR's Sam Greenglass reports
NTSB confirms business jet broke apart before crashing near West Palm Beach, killing nine
